newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECHS PUT ON BRAVE FACE DESPITE LOSS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECHS PUT ON BRAVE FACE DESPITE LOSS.

text.p: Czech soccer put on a brave face on Thursday following a crucial World Cup qualifier loss to Yugoslavia, invoking the run-up to last year's European championship as proof the country can bounce back.
The Czechs lost 2-1 to Yugoslavia on Wednesday. A last minute goal from Aston Villa's Savo Milosevic severely damaged Czech hopes of qualifying for France in 1998.

With only four points from four games the beaten Euro 96 finalists are on the brink of elimination. Yugoslavia have 15 points from six matches, one fewer than group leaders Spain while Slovakia are third on 12 points.
Only the top team in each group is guaranteed a spot in the World Cup.

But Czech coach Dusan Uhrin said the Czechs have been down this road before following a demoralising loss to Luxembourg in the Euro 96 qualifying round, only to storm back by beating Norway and the Netherlands to win the group.
"After the loss to Luxembourg, it looked like the end and that we could not qualify but in the end we all know what happened," Uhrin said.
What clearly is not happening for the Czechs is goal-scoring.
At Euro 96, they scored goals at key moments while their opponents faltered. Now the boot is on the other foot.
"We will have to work for a miracle," Kaiserslautern striker Pavel Kuka said after the defeat.
Striker Martin Frydek said: "We have to fight to the end just like last year but to move on it will take a lot of luck."
